stories.headline: Meta delays new business terms to Nov. 20 after publisher pushback
stories.subtitle: Meta pushed its revised Commercial Terms from Oct. 30 to Nov. 20 after publishers and Sen. Marsha Blackburn warned the crawling language could sweep up creators' content. Meta says the terms cover ads and business products only.

stories.headline: Federal class action alleges glasses recorded chats without 'Hey Meta'
stories.subtitle: Subia v. Meta, filed Oct. 19 in California, alleges AI glasses recorded conversations with no wake phrase. No class is certified and nothing is decided; Meta previously said the issue is resolved, and voice logs can be reviewed in the Meta AI app.

stories.headline: Smart glasses boom faces tougher regulatory scrutiny in Europe
stories.subtitle: Europe's data protection board says Ray-Ban Meta-style glasses 'facilitate covert recording,' Reuters reports, with Italy and Austria investigating school incidents. Advocacy group NOYB urges coordinated restrictions — expect customers to raise this.

stories.headline: Camera-free Ray-Ban Meta Audio glasses on sale from $349
stories.subtitle: Meta's first audio-only glasses have no camera, weigh 43 grams, and run up to 12 hours (48 more from the case) with open-ear audio, calls, and Meta AI. In Clubmaster and Burbank styles — for shoppers who want AI glasses without a camera.

stories.headline: SanDisk named exclusive storage partner for Meta VR Glasses
stories.subtitle: SanDisk's official microSD Express cards and USB-C drives will arrive alongside the $1,299.99 VR Glasses in spring 2027. No pricing or capacities yet — expect customers to ask about expansion for the glasses' media-heavy use cases.
